new_statements.quote: Focus is marked by several manual prosodic parameters in both RSL and NGT. Focused signs can be longer, larger, slower, and/or higher, and they may contain more repetitions than their non-focused version. In addition, we have seen that RSL and NGT differ from each other. RSL uses repetitions more frequently for focus marking than NGT, and NGT uses size modification more frequently than RSL. [p. 113] … As for the manual prosodic markers, no modality effects can be found. […] The mechanism that sign languages employ for the same function is completely parallel: movement (or location) of the sign is modified in order to make a sign more prominent perceptually. [pp. 222-223]

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has no record and no existing statement for russ1255. This work adds a domain statement: RSL has focus-driven manual prosodic prominence (phrase/sentence level) realised by longer, larger, slower, higher or repeated movement; it gives no word-level placement, so it cannot support a fixed/weight/lexical reading.
new_statements.rule_in_words: 'Stress' in this work is sentence-level prosodic prominence that marks the focused constituent: in RSL a focused sign is made longer, larger, slower and/or higher, or given extra repetitions, relative to its unfocused form (length in 64% of 149 RSL focus tokens). The author treats this as the sign-modality parallel of pitch-based sentence stress in spoken languages. Nothing is said about stress placement inside a sign (word level), and no claim is made that RSL lacks word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: p. 113: in RSL the repetition marker is restricted by movement type ('only signs with hand-internal and small path movement can be affected by this marker'); type of movement significantly influences height marking only in RSL; no differences by syntactic role (subject/object/verb) for any focus marker; information focus was the most marked focus type. p. 29 (sec. 2.3.2, on ASL, not RSL): Petronio (1991) and Wilbur (1997) claim ASL stress has a fixed clause-final position, cited as background only.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog russ1255 is labelled 'Russian-Tajik Sign Language'; every opened work describes Russian Sign Language (RSL) as used in Russia (thesis ch. 1 notes RSL is used over a very large area with low lexical variation per Burkova & Varinova 2012; the focus study used ten RSL signers). No work mentions Tajik Sign Language or any Tajik variety.

sources.citation: Kimmelman, Vadim. 2014. Information Structure in Russian Sign Language and Sign Language of the Netherlands. PhD dissertation, Universiteit van Amsterdam (ACLC). 290 pp. hdl 11245/1.432175
sources.note: 'Stress' treated only as prosodic focus marking: sec. 2.3.2 'Prosodic/stress marking' (pp.29-30) reviews stress-as-focus in ASL/DGS/NGT (stressed signs longer, larger, faster); ch.4 and sec. 7.4.1 (p.223) report RSL focus is marked by manual prosodic prominence (modified movement/location of the focused sign). No statement about word-level stress placement; no claim that RSL has or lacks lexical stress.
